observations: Photo 0: one white electric dry iron standing on its heel on a tiled floor, with a cloth-covered power cord and a 3-pin UK-type plug.
The plastic body is grubby and scuffed; the temperature dial is visible but no brand or model is legible.
The cloth cord is frayed and dirty, with a frayed fabric end at the iron and at least one spliced or taped joint where coloured inner wires appear exposed.
No steam tank or water filler is visible, consistent with a dry iron.
The soleplate is not shown; no photo shows the iron plugged in or heating.
No receipt or warranty card appears in the photo.

claims.claim: Used dry pressing iron, still working
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a dry iron, but nothing shows it heating; no clip or photo of it plugged in with the light on.

claims.claim: Barely used, bought new last year
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a heavily soiled body and a frayed, spliced cord, which is long hard use, not a barely used iron.
Photo 0 shows a frayed cord with a taped or spliced joint and exposed wire, a visible fault and a shock hazard.
A dry iron has no motor; the statement cannot be checked and does not describe this item.

risks.risk: Heating element or thermostat dead, so the iron does not heat or overheats.
risks.proof: A clip of the iron plugged in, indicator light on, then pressing a damp cloth or showing a water drop sizzle on the soleplate.

risks.risk: Damaged and spliced cord with exposed wire, unsafe to use.
risks.proof: A close photo of the full cord length and the splice, or of a replacement cord fitted.
A close photo of the soleplate face in good light.

proof_requests: A clip of the iron plugged in with the indicator light on and heating a damp cloth.
A close photo of the soleplate face.
A close photo of the whole cord including the taped joint.
A photo of the brand and rating label, usually on the heel or underside.
response.reason: It is clearly a used electric dry iron and can be priced by type at its worst case, as not working with a damaged cord; the 'barely used' and 'no fault' claims are contradicted by the worn body and spliced cord in photo 0.
